# Naka Lambda dependencies (data plane: app_agent.py, control plane:
# app_control.py, plus everything they import). Generated by grepping
# every top-level `import`/`from` across the project's *.py files.
#
# boto3 / botocore are DELIBERATELY NOT listed here. The Lambda python3.12
# managed runtime already ships a boto3/botocore on sys.path, and every
# module in this project (ledger.py, audit.py, normalize.py, detect.py,
# app_control.py) imports boto3 lazily inside a function precisely so the
# runtime's copy is what gets used. Bundling our own would just add ~35 MB
# of dead weight to the zip for zero behavioural change, unless a specific
# API shape is required that the runtime's version doesn't have yet -- if
# that ever happens, pin boto3/botocore here explicitly and say why.
#
# fixtures/build_kyc_sheet.py needs `reportlab` and `Pillow`, but that
# script is a one-time, dev-time fixture generator (see its own docstring)
# -- its outputs (kyc-sheet-tkt-4471.pdf, kyc-sheet-tkt-4472.png) are
# already committed under fixtures/, and neither app_agent.py nor
# app_control.py imports it at runtime. Not included here on purpose.

# The Strands Agents SDK: `Agent`, `S3SessionManager`,
# `CedarAuthorization`, the intervention/hook types used throughout
# guard.py, audit.py and rehydrate.py.
#
# This is ALSO provided by the prebuilt Lambda layer named in the PRD
# (arn:aws:lambda:ap-south-1:856699698935:layer:strands-agents-py3_12-aarch64:<v>,
# wired up in deploy/deploy.sh). It's still pinned here so
# `pip install -r requirements.txt` gives a complete, runnable local dev
# environment (e.g. for running selfcheck.py) without needing that layer
# at all. For the Lambda zip itself this is redundant with the layer, not
# wrong: Lambda resolves same-named packages from /var/task (the function
# package) before /opt/python (a layer), so having both just means the
# zip's copy wins. That is NOT harmless if the zip's copy is older than
# the layer's, which is exactly what happened once here -- see
# deploy/build.sh's comment on pip's marker evaluation.
#
# >=1.44.0, not >=1.0.0: `strands.vended_interventions.cedar`
# (CedarAuthorization, the whole Q1 path in app_agent.py) does not exist
# before 1.44.0. Verified by inspecting the published wheels: 1.42.0 has no
# vended_interventions package at all, 1.44.0 does. The prebuilt Lambda
# layer (version 2 = strands-agents 1.40.0) therefore CANNOT supply this
# either -- bundling it here is required, not an optimisation.
strands-agents>=1.44.0

# Cedar policy evaluator -- the only third-party package app_control.py
# imports directly (cedarpy.PolicySet.from_str for validating a PUT'd
# policy), and the engine behind cedar_q2.py's Q2/Q3 decisions. PRD
# confirms 4.12.0 ships manylinux2014 wheels for x86_64 *and* aarch64,
# Python 3.10-3.14 -- pin at least that version so
# `--only-binary=:all:` (see deploy/build.sh) has something to resolve
# against on arm64.
cedarpy>=4.12.0

# normalize.py's xlsx branch (`from openpyxl import load_workbook`),
# read-only usage only (load_workbook(..., read_only=True, data_only=True)).
openpyxl>=3.1.0
